summary: Customer confused which region is impacted during incident; requests region-specific status indicators (us-east vs eu-west)
description:
Customer (HelioDesk, Inc.) reports confusion during a recent degraded performance window: they observed elevated 5xx + timeouts from eu-west client traffic, but the public status page showed a generic "API Degraded Performance" without region scoping. Customer is asking whether Redwood can indicate affected regions (us-east vs us-west vs eu-west) and whether they should fail over.

Context:
- Customer runs multi-region clients (primary: eu-west, secondary: us-east).
- They use Redwood Hosted API with a region-pinned base URL for most services but have some traffic routed through a global endpoint.

Customer questions:
1) "Was this incident eu-west only or global?"
2) "How should we know when to fail over regions?"
3) "Can your status page show region-specific components so our on-call can make decisions without opening a ticket?"

Impact (customer-reported):
- ~15–25 min window of intermittent failures.
- Higher impact on streaming requests; embeddings also saw elevated latency.

What we need to do:
- Confirm region scope for incident INC-2024-06-18-1432 (and whether eu-west was actually impacted vs spillover).
- Provide guidance on how to interpret Redwood status + what customer can do now.
- Feed request into status page transparency upgrades (region-level components / clearer comms).
comments:
2024-06-18 09:12 PT — Dev Patel (Support Ops) — Intake
Customer reached out via support portal.

Customer quote:
"Your status page said 'API degraded' but didn't say which region. Our eu-west traffic was failing, but us-east looked mostly OK. We can't tell whether to fail over or if the issue is global. Can you add region-specific status?"

Requested artifacts:
- Request IDs for failed calls
- Approx time window + their region configuration

2024-06-18 09:26 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Escalation Liaison) — First response to customer
Thanks — we can help clarify. If you share a few request IDs + timestamps we can confirm region scope and whether failures were isolated.

In the meantime:
- If you are using the global endpoint, you can pin traffic to a specific region base URL.
- For retry behavior, use exponential backoff and consider temporary fallback to a secondary region if you see sustained 5xx/timeouts.

We’re also actively improving our public status page to reflect region-specific impact when applicable; I’ll follow up with what we find for this incident.

- Window: 08:37–09:02 PT
- Affected endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (streaming=true) and /v1/embeddings
- Example request IDs: rwd_req_01J0Z9K8Q2A3P5, rwd_req_01J0Z9M1X4N7T8
- Their client region: eu-west (primary). Some traffic uses a global hostname due to an older deployment.

2024-06-18 09:55 PT — Owen Phillips — Internal triage
Looping in SRE to confirm region scope for INC-2024-06-18-1432.

Posted in Slack #incidents:
- Asking whether incident was us-east capacity/routing related and whether eu-west errors were secondary (retries, global endpoint routing, or shared control-plane).

Notes:

2024-06-18 10:18 PT — Christine Wong (Status transparency implementation) — Internal note
Checked draft incident comms: status update was posted under a single broad "API" component because we don't yet expose region components publicly.

This ticket is directly addressed by the region-level component breakdown work in flight (Linear ENG-4823).

2024-06-18 10:33 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE Mgr) — SRE findings
INC-2024-06-18-1432 was primarily a us-east serving capacity degradation due to a routing policy issue (spike in queue depth -> elevated 5xx/timeouts). eu-west cluster health was normal.

However, customers using the global endpoint may have had a subset of traffic routed to us-east during the event due to their account routing policy + retry behavior.

Recommendation for customer:
- Prefer region-pinned hostname if they want deterministic region behavior.
- If using global, ensure their policy is configured to prefer eu-west and only fail over on sustained failures.

External comms:
- We should have labeled this as "Hosted API Serving — us-east" (future state) plus note that global endpoint users may be impacted.

2024-06-18 10:46 PT — Owen Phillips — Response to customer (with incident scope)
We confirmed the incident scope:
- Primary impact was in our us-east serving region.
- Our eu-west serving region was healthy during the window.

Why you may have seen eu-west client impact:
- If any of your traffic is hitting our global endpoint, requests can fail over to another region based on routing policy and retry/fallback behavior. During the us-east degradation window, those requests could have encountered elevated errors/timeouts.

Actions you can take now:
1) Pin your hostname/base URL to eu-west for critical paths if you want deterministic region selection.
2) Keep a secondary region configured (us-west/us-east) and fail over only when you see sustained error rate above your threshold.
3) For streaming, use retry with backoff on connection interruptions; if streaming is your main user path, consider temporarily switching to non-streaming during a streaming-specific degradation.

On your request for region-specific status:
Yes — this is something we're actively rolling out. Our current public status page does not always communicate region scope clearly for partial degradations. We’re upgrading it to include region-level components (e.g., Hosted API Serving — us-east / us-west / eu-west) so you can make failover decisions without opening a ticket.

If you’d like, we can also review your routing policy/settings with you to ensure global endpoint behavior matches your expectations.

2024-06-19 08:05 PT — Customer (HelioDesk) — Follow-up
Thanks, that helps. Two requests:
1) Please share best practice for deciding when to fail over (how to interpret degraded vs partial outage).
2) Can you notify us when the region-specific status components go live?

2024-06-19 09:02 PT — Owen Phillips — Best-practice guidance + notification offer
Failover guidance (practical):
- Treat sustained 5xx/timeouts over ~3–5 minutes as a trigger to fail over for user-facing flows.
- For degraded performance (higher latency but low error rate), we recommend staying on the primary region unless you’re exceeding your own latency SLO for a sustained window.
- If we publish a workaround in the status update (e.g., "pin to eu-west"), use that as the first mitigation before region failover.

We can notify you:
- I’ve added you to our update list for when region-level status components roll out.
- In the interim, if you see ambiguity in a status event, we can confirm scope quickly via this ticket or your CSM.

Internal: syncing with docs owner to ensure public docs clarify region pinning + global endpoint behavior.

2024-06-20 11:24 PT — Elliot Price (Documentation) — Internal note
Added to backlog for public docs update (in progress in redwood-docs/pr_922): "How to read our status page" will include guidance on region-scoped incidents and the difference between global endpoint vs region-pinned hostname.

Once region components are live, we’ll update the status page glossary accordingly.

2024-06-21 09:40 PT — Owen Phillips — Closing note to customer
We’re going to close this ticket as the immediate question (region scope for the incident) is resolved.

Summary:
- Incident impact was us-east; eu-west was healthy.
- Your eu-west client saw impact likely due to some traffic using the global endpoint and routing/failover behavior.

Next steps on our side:
- Rolling out region-level status components so future incidents can be communicated as "Serving — us-east" vs global.
- Publishing updated guidance on interpreting the status page and when to fail over.

If you’d like, send us your current endpoint configuration and we can sanity-check it to ensure your traffic is pinned as intended.
resolution: Provided incident scope confirmation (us-east primary impact; eu-west healthy) and customer guidance on region pinning and failover decisioning. Logged request as input to status page transparency upgrades; region-level component rollout planned (ENG-4823) and docs update in progress (redwood-docs/pr_922).
